result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.

Here's the full picture for Transformer 1 at MAIN:

## Open / Pending-Approval Work Orders (Transformer 1, MAIN)

Only one exists:

| # | Description | Priority | Scheduled Date | De-energize? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1000051** | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | **1** | *(no schedstart; note field says target start 2024-01-19, 0 other WOs at MAIN that day)* | **Yes – outage required** (internal OLTC work) |

## Bundling

Fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist (only one total, and it's the only outage work), so **no bundle can be formed** — per the rule, nothing is bundled. There is no "earliest possible date vs. calendar load" comparison to make across a bundle, and no total planned hours need aggregating.

## Latest Gas Readings (2024-01-19)

- **Acetylene (C2H2): 7 ppm** — above the 1 ppm threshold, consistent with the OLTC/coking concern and a thermal T2 signature
- **Hydrogen (H2): 2,850 ppm** — very elevated

The high acetylene confirms active arcing/thermal activity in the tap changer, matching the P1 severity already assigned to the work order.

## Recommendation

**WO 1000051 should be done alone, not deferred.**

Reasons:
- **Acetylene at 7 ppm is well above threshold**, and hydrogen at 2,850 ppm signals significant in-service distress. Deferring to "the next planned outage" risks letting contact wear/coking progress toward a fault while energized.
- The work order is already **Priority 1**, not routine/schedulable work that can wait.
- Since no other outage-needing work orders exist, there's no efficiency to gain by waiting — bundling would only add delay without reducing total outages.
- If any new outage-needing work orders emerge later (e.g., electrical testing, internal inspection), they can be evaluated then against their own dates and this unit's DGA trend; if acetylene stays above 1 ppm, that future inspection work should also be pulled to the earliest date rather than deferred.

**Suggested action:** approve and schedule WO 1000051 for the earliest feasible date (the note indicates 2024-01-19 had 0 other scheduled work orders at MAIN, so calendar load is not a constraint).
